explanation: Place one queen per row. For every trial column, compare with earlier queens: equal columns conflict, and equal absolute row/column differences share a diagonal. Recurse only for safe prefixes.
timeComplexity: O(n²·n! + nS) conservative upper bound: at most O(n!) valid distinct-column prefixes, each trying n columns and checking up to n earlier queens; S complete placements each copy n entries.
spaceComplexity: O(n) working placement and recursion frames, plus O(nS) copied output entries for S solutions. Python additionally creates an O(n) temporary prefix slice while checking a row.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/n_queens.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Earlier rows are already nonattacking. A new queen can attack an earlier one only through an equal column or a diagonal where |columnDifference|=rowDifference; the validity check rejects exactly these cases. Trying every surviving column covers every legal board, and copying a completed placement protects it from later backtracking.
walkthrough: For n=4, choose row columns 1 then 3. In row 2, column 0 is safe; row 3 then accepts column 2, yielding [1,3,0,2]. The symmetric branch yields [2,0,3,1]. Other branches fail a column/diagonal check.
edgeCases: A placement lists columns in increasing row order.
Boards of size 2 and 3 have no solutions.
Each output placement is copied before backtracking changes the working list.
